device.description: 16-bit 250 kSPS sampling ADC, +/-10 V input, 16-bit or byte-wide parallel bus with R/C, BYTE and BUSY
device.note: ads8505.pdf (SLAS180B) p.3 electrical characteristics (logic levels, binary twos complement, bus access/relinquish 83 ns, VDIG 4.75-5.25 V), p.4 DB/DW pinout, p.5 terminal functions, p.9 starting a conversion, Table 1 control line functions, p.10 reading data, Table 2 output codes, p.11 Table 3 conversion timing, Figure 22 bit locations vs BYTE

notModeled: analog input (+/-10 V), internal/external reference and CAP: the result is always the 0 V code 0000h (twos complement)

byte mode (Figure 22): BYTE high puts bits 7..0 on pins 6-13 and bits 15..8 on pins 15-22 (pin 15 = bit 15 ... pin 22 = bit 8), i.e. the two bytes swapped; the model's high-BYTE pattern follows the figure

conversion start: CS and R/C are internally ORed and level triggered (both low >= 40 ns starts conversion n, whichever falls last); the model starts one on every R/C falling edge and ignores a start by CS falling while R/C is low
a new convert command while BUSY is low aborts the conversion in progress and resets the ADC (Table 1, Figure 26)
reading the previous result during a conversion (valid up to t2 after the start) and invalid data from then until BUSY rises: the model always outputs the 0 V code while R/C is high and CS is low
BUSY delays tpd 25 ns / td1, acquisition time 1.8 us, convert pulse width 40-1750 ns, VDIG <= VANA
variants: single-device datasheet; pin-compatible with ADS7805 (100 kSPS) and the 12-bit ADS8504. DB (SSOP) and DW (SOIC) share the pin numbering.
